div.head: III Atr 1.2
div.ab: And þæt grið, þæt man sylleð on I burhgaþinðe, bete man þæt mid VI hundr̄; and þær man sylle on wǽpentáke, bete man þæt mid hundr̄, gif hit man brecð; and þæt man syllé on éalahuse, bete man þæt æt deadum menn mid VI healfmarce ⁊ æt cwicon mid XII óran.

Et pax que dabitur in unius burgi þincþa, emendetur VI hund'; et ubi dabitur in wapentako, emendetur infracta pax I hundreto; et pax que dabitur in ealahus, emendetur de homine occiso sex dimidiis marcis, de uiuo duodecim oris.

And þæt grið þæt man sylleð on I burhgaþinðe, bete man þæt mid VI hundr̄; and þæ[t] man sylle on wǽpentáke, bete man þæt mid hundr̄, gif hit man brecð; and þæt man sylle on éalahuse, bete man þæt æt deadum menn mid VI healfmarce ⁊ æt cwicon mid XII óran.

Und der Friedensschutz, der gegeben wird im Gericht Einer Stadt, den büsse man mit 6 Hundert; und der im Wapentake gegeben wird, den büsse man mit 1 Hundert, wenn man ihn bricht; und der im Bierhause gegeben wird, den büsse man, [wenn man da] einen Menschen erschlagen, mit 6 Halbmark, und [wenn Angegriffener] lebt, mit 12 Ör.

And the protection which is given in the court of a single borough, let it be compensated with 6 hundred; and that which is given in the wapentake, let it be compensated with 1 hundred, if it is broken; and that which is given in an alehouse, let it be compensated, [if] a person [is] killed [there], with 6 half-marks, and [if the person attacked] lives, with 12 ores.

And for breach of the peace established in the court of one borough 600 [of silver] shall be paid as compensation, and 100 for that established in a wapentake. In the case of breach of the peace in an ale-house, 6 half marks shall be paid as compensation if a man is slain, and 12 ores if no-one is slain.

And the peace which is given in the meeting of one borough is to be atoned for with six hundred; and that which is given in a wapentake, is to be atoned for with a hundred, if it is broken; and that which is given in an alehouse, is to be atoned for, if a man is killed, with six half marks, and if no one is killed, with twelve ores.

Vermutlich ist nicht das Gericht jeder Stadt (s. d. Gl 13) Englands oder auch nur der Denalagu, sondern bloss des Fünfburgenbunds gemeint.—Unter Biergelage (s. d. Gl 5. 7e) wird mitverstanden die Gilde; s. Gl Genossenschaft 8; Wapentake 8

Probably what is meant is not the court of every borough (see that word in Gl 13) in England, or even just in the Danelaw, but only of the confederation of the Five Boroughs.—Under ale-feast (see that word in Gl 5. 7e) the gild is also to be understood; see Gl Genossenschaft 8; Wapentake 8

Voller Friedbruch kostet nochmal soviel wie Halbverletzung; s. d. Gl 2. 3.—Die 6 Halbmark (s. d. Gl 3b) stehen auch u. 3, 2. 12 neben ihrer Hälfte, den 12 Ör, dem gewöhnlichen Strafgeldfixum (s. d. Gl 21), das ‘Rechtsbruchbusse’ (s. d. Gl 7) der Denalagu heisst

Full breach of the peace costs twice as much as half-violation; see that word in Gl 2. 3.—The 6 half-marks (see that word in Gl 3b) also appear below 3, 2. 12 alongside their half, the 12 ores, the usual fixed fine (see that word in Gl 21), which in the Danelaw is called ‘compensation for breach of law’ (see that word in Gl 7)

Q’s translation (see p. 64¹) points to a reading on anre burhge geþincðe, cf. the reading of H.

The fines throughout this law are stated according to Danish standards, cf. A. and G. 2 and E. and G. passim. The mark (mörk) contained 8 oran (aurar), while the ora (eyrir) contained sometimes 16, sometimes 20 pence, see IV Atr. 9, 2 and note.
Cf. VIII Atr. 4.
